newsitem.title: USA: November trial for Pakistani in CIA shooting case.
newsitem.headline: November trial for Pakistani in CIA shooting case.

text.p: A judge on Wednesday set a Nov. 3 trial date for a Pakistani man accused of killing two CIA workers and wounding three others in a 1993 shooting spree outside the spy agency's headquarters.

At a hearing conducted under unusually tight security, Fairfax Circuit Court Judge J. Howe Brown rejected a defence request for even more time to prepare for the trial of Mir Aimal Kansi, who sat silently throughout the proceeding.
The judge also denied a request from news organisations to televise the trial, saying he wanted Kansi to get a fair trial and was concerned about the safety of witnesses who testified.

And he denied a broad request from defence attorneys for a so-called gag order that would have barred the FBI, CIA and State Department from commenting on any of the evidence or the substance of the case.
Kansi, 33, was apprehended in Pakistan and brought back to the United States last month to face murder and other criminal charges that carry the death penalty.

He has been charged in the Jan. 25, 1993, morning rush hour shooting outside Central Intelligence Agency headquarters at Langley, Virginia, just outside Washington. All but one of the victims were CIA employees.

Defence attorney Richard Goemann had told the court he needed at least 10 months to prepare for trial, saying he would have to go to Pakistan to interview witnesses and would need documents from the CIA, FBI and other agencies.
The bearded Kansi sat throughout the hearing with security guards close by him.
